terms.proofCondition: Settled cash of at least 8000 USD received within 45 days

strategy.title: No plan until a purchase price for the eligibility workbook is established
strategy.why: The card's $2,000 'price' is the state grant programme's payment to providers per unserved location they connect (programme guidelines, Oct 2026). That is a grant award to the buyer, not what a provider pays for an eligibility workbook. No price a buyer pays for the workbook is recorded, so OFFER_AND_PRICE is not established, and the deal count against the $8,000 target cannot be computed. Everything else (75 reachable providers, 8/60 paid conversion, Brain-produced spreadsheet, $20 cost, $0 exposure, 10-day settlement in a 45-day window) is on the card.

alternatives.title: Sell at $2,000 per workbook
alternatives.why: Reads a grant payout per connected location as a purchase price; rejected. At the measured 8/60 conversion the 75-provider list yields about 10 sales, so the plan works only if the real price is at least about $800 - which nothing yet shows.

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is the right stance and the disagreement with Brain's price link is correct. The card's price fact is the state broadband grant programme paying providers up to $2,000 per unserved location they connect (programme guidelines, Oct 2026): a grant the state pays the buyer, not an amount any provider pays for an eligibility workbook. Brain's OFFER_AND_PRICE link ('price 2000 USD (EVIDENCE)') rests on that fact, so its price carries the NOT_A_PURCHASE defect. Every other link is on evidence: 75 providers on the eligible-applicant list, 8/60 = 13.3% paid conversion on this offer's own sales, Brain-produced spreadsheet, $20 cost, $0 exposure, 10 days to cash inside 45. Recomputed: 75 x 8/60 = 10 expected sales, so the target needs a real price of at least $8,000 / 10 = $800 per workbook (more for margin against variance) — nothing on the card shows it. The revision names OFFER_AND_PRICE as decisive, does not treat the $2,000 as known, keeps the ledger empty and gives a concrete resolution (amounts paid on the 8 recorded orders, or published dated prices for eligibility analyses sold to WISPs).
findings: Price defect on Brain's established price: NOT_A_PURCHASE — the $2,000 is a grant per connected location paid by the state to providers (a reward to the buyer), not a purchase price for the workbook.

Arithmetic verified: 75 x 0.1333 = 10 expected paid orders; breakeven price for $8,000 is $800 per workbook; at $2,000 Brain would need 4-5 deals, which is why reading the grant as a price inflates the plan.
The 8 earlier paid orders necessarily carried an actual amount; retrieving it is the cheapest resolution and research step r1 targets it first.

Stance check: missing evidence, not a constraint — correctly no constraint is claimed; not CONDITIONAL, since the price behind existing orders is a retrievable record, not something only a live test measures.
